holidays.name: National Chocolate-Covered Nuts Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in almonds, peanuts, cashews, and other nuts dunked in rich chocolate. It is the snack aisle's answer to the eternal question of whether you want something healthy or something delicious, solved by having both.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it grew out of food-industry promotion and was spread by calendar-keeping websites. There is no single official founder or government proclamation.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate-covered nuts are a descendant of the 'dragée' tradition, in which French confectioners coated almonds in sugar and chocolate centuries ago.

holidays.name: National Clam Chowder Day
holidays.description: A salute to the creamy, briny soup in which clams, potatoes, and onions swim together. People argue passionately about whether it should be white and creamy or red and tomato-based.
holidays.origin: Chowder has been a New England staple since the 1700s, and the day is an unofficial food observance kept by food fans and restaurants.
holidays.funFact: In 1939, a Maine bill was introduced to make it illegal to put tomatoes in clam chowder, a debate that still stirs strong feelings in New England.

holidays.name: Open That Bottle Night
holidays.description: A night dedicated to finally uncorking that special bottle of wine you have been saving for the perfect occasion, because the perfect occasion might never come. You are encouraged to share it with friends and tell the story behind it.
holidays.origin: It was created in 2000 by Wall Street Journal wine columnists Dorothy Gaiter and John Brecher, who suggested the last Saturday of February as the date. Many people now celebrate it on a fixed date.
holidays.funFact: The columnists came up with the idea after hearing from readers who were afraid to open their prized bottles, only to find out later that the wine had gone bad.

holidays.name: Quiet Day
holidays.description: A day of peace and calm, in which you are invited to put the phone down, mute the noise, and enjoy some silence. Introverts and tired parents celebrate it with particular enthusiasm.
holidays.origin: It is an informal awareness observance that has circulated among wellness and holiday calendars as a reminder to unplug from the constant din of modern life.
holidays.funFact: Studies suggest that just two minutes of silence can be more relaxing than listening to calming music.

holidays.name: Pistol Patent Day
holidays.description: A day commemorating the date Samuel Colt received his first patent for a revolver design, a landmark event in firearm and manufacturing history that also changed the American West and Hollywood Westerns.
holidays.origin: Samuel Colt was granted a US patent for his revolving-cylinder firearm on February 25, 1836, and went on to found Colt's Patent Fire Arms Manufacturing Company in Paterson, New Jersey.
holidays.funFact: Colt's first factory in Paterson, New Jersey, went bankrupt within a few years, but he rebounded and later became a pioneer of mass production and advertising.
